items.title: October Patch Tuesday: record 1,400+ fixes, with a Windows Shell Mark-of-the-Web bypass already exploited
items.summary: Microsoft's October release patches roughly 1,411 flaws, the largest batch it has shipped, including 70 rated critical. CVE-2026-96951, a command-injection bug in Windows Shell, lets a crafted file skip Mark-of-the-Web, so SmartScreen and Protected View warnings never appear; it is being used in attacks and CISA added it to KEV on October 13. Two other bugs were public before the fix: a .NET Framework flaw that can sidestep WDAC (found by Google Project Zero) and a MessagePack-CSharp denial of service. Push the October cumulative updates first to endpoints where users open email and web downloads, and note that Windows 11 24H2 Home/Pro has now reached end of updates.

items.title: Three chained Ivanti Connect Secure zero-days gave an attacker root on a patched VPN; one bug still has no fix
items.summary: Volexity found an actor it tracks as UTA0576 chaining an authentication bypass and RCE (tracked together as CVE-2026-104935) with an unnamed privilege-escalation bug to get unauthenticated root on an up-to-date Ivanti Connect Secure appliance, starting October 3. The intruder stole domain credentials stored on the box, hunted for LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, sprayed passwords and wiped logs. Fixed builds include 22.8R2.5, 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0 and 25.1.3.1, but the root-escalation fix is still weeks away and CISA has added the flaw to KEV. Upgrade now, hunt for repeated requests to /dana-na/auth/url_default/welcome.cgi, a mismatched X-DSCGI-PATH header, the /data/.icscap/ directory and traffic to 108.165.147[.]64, and rotate any credentials the appliance held; Volexity says Ivanti's Integrity Checker misses this chain.

items.title: npm Trusted Publishing trusted repo names, not IDs, leaving 1,500+ packages open to takeover
items.summary: Bloom Security showed that npm's Trusted Publishing bound a package to a GitHub owner/repo name rather than GitHub's permanent numeric IDs, so after a rename, transfer or deletion anyone could re-register that name, add a matching workflow and publish a release that even carried valid provenance. Over 1,500 packages with more than 10 million total downloads were exposed, and the researchers say GitLab's integration has the same weakness; whether it was abused is unknown. GitHub has shipped changes, including expiring unvalidated bindings after 48 hours. Maintainers should run `npm trust list`, re-create any binding that points to a renamed or moved repo, and remove bindings before deleting a repo; consumers should check that a package's provenance names the expected repository.

items.title: Docker Hub 'GhostPat' bug let personal tokens keep push rights after an account became an organization
items.summary: From August 2024 until a September 30 fix, converting a personal Docker Hub account into an organization moved its personal access tokens to the named owner without changing the secret, so whoever held an old token could push, pull or delete images as that owner. Docker says a review of about 304,000 pushes made with transferred tokens found no misuse, has deactivated the transferred tokens it identified, and now requires consent before someone is named an organization owner. No client update is needed, but revoke unrecognized PATs, check for organizations you did not knowingly join, rotate credentials if Docker emailed you, and move CI automation to organization access tokens.

items.title: Meta says attackers with an employee's stolen credentials took code and some personal data from its GitHub repos
items.summary: Meta is notifying about 1,500 people, mostly US staff, after an outside group used one employee's stolen credentials to reach some of its GitHub repositories. Most of what was taken was product source code, but about 1% was personal data that had been committed to repos against policy, much of it synthetic test data. Meta cut off access, rotated secrets found in the repos and is adding scanning to catch personal data uploads. The lesson for AppSec teams: enforce phishing-resistant MFA and short-lived tokens for source-control access, and run secret and PII scanning on every repository, not just production ones.

items.title: Anthropic red team: small open-weight models are close to copying themselves across cheap IoT boxes
items.summary: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team tested whether models can stand up their own inference on unfamiliar hardware, running a 26B open-weight model split across 15 cheap Android TV boxes and a 9B model on eight of nine device types. In a closed lab of eight emulated devices with exploitation kept deliberately trivial, only GLM-5.2 completed the full replicate-and-spread cycle, while models of 30B or fewer parameters still fail at chaining the steps; Anthropic expects them to catch up within months. Such an AI worm would be slow and compute-poor but hard to switch off. Defenders and ISPs should watch for large model-weight transfers and unusual device-to-device traffic, and default credentials on IoT gear remain the main door to close.

items.title: An AI agent with environment context changed the severity of three in four 'HIGH' cloud findings
items.summary: Sola Security researchers had an agent re-grade 9,967 HIGH-severity findings from two commercial cloud security platforms across eight production environments; it downgraded 58.5% and upgraded 16.6%, most often downgrading resources that were orphaned or attached to nothing. Read-only probes confirmed the agent's facts 99.4% of the time where they could be checked, but only 81.8% if unverifiable cases are counted as wrong, and the study did not test whether its grades predict real attacks. For teams piloting AI triage, the takeaway is to require proof that every exploit path is blocked before a downgrade, verify the agent's evidence against the live environment, and keep humans in charge of any automated fixes.
